verdict.rationale: A is the more faithful extraction of the original implementation, retaining both the pricing evaluation order and the reservation list used for rollback. B offers substantially better characterization tests and stronger type annotations, but its payment-decline cleanup uses the current order.items rather than the recorded reservations, changing behavior if the item list changes during charging. For a production refactor explicitly requiring unchanged behavior, I narrowly prefer A; B's characterization tests would be valuable additions.
a_issues: Adds no regression tests despite gaps in the existing coverage around pricing boundaries, partial rollback, and notification failures.
Reservation-related helper parameters use bare list annotations instead of list[Item].
Extracting the one-line shipping expression into a separate helper adds little readability.
b_issues: Payment-decline rollback releases order.items instead of the original reservation snapshot. If the list changes during charging, this can release unreserved items or leave reservations outstanding.
Pricing now traverses items twice and calculates the subtotal before looking up the tax rate, rather than preserving the original single-pass evaluation order.

verdict.rationale: B more faithfully preserves the original implementation, particularly the captured reservation list used to roll back a declined payment. A adds substantially better regression coverage, but releases the current order.items instead of the actual reservations, which can change behavior if a collaborator modifies the item list during checkout. Given the explicit production requirement to preserve behavior, I narrowly prefer B, though its lack of additional characterization tests is a significant weakness.
a_issues: Payment-decline rollback uses order.items rather than the captured reservation list. If the list changes during a gateway call, rollback can release unreserved items or leave reservations outstanding.
Pricing now traverses items twice and recomputes line prices rather than retaining the original single-pass calculation; this is unnecessary churn for a behavior-preserving extraction.
b_issues: Adds no characterization tests despite the existing suite lacking coverage for several important pricing, partial-rollback, and notification-failure cases.
Uses unparameterized list annotations for reservations, and _charge has a long six-argument signature.
